q: Random circuit sampling (as implemented in Google's quantum supremacy experiment, 2019) aims to sample from the output distribution of a random quantum circuit. The classical hardness of this task is based on:
opts: Proven lower bounds on circuit depth
The conjectural hardness of computing output probabilities of random circuits (anticoncentration and average-case hardness of computing amplitudes)
exp: The hardness of classical simulation of random circuit sampling is not proven but based on: (1) anticoncentration of output probabilities (distributed like Porter-Thomas), (2) average-case hardness of computing amplitudes (related to #P-hardness), and (3) the assumption that worst-case and average-case hardness are equivalent for this problem.
